title: a @throws {never} marker makes the call safe, not the expression that selects the callee: five selector spellings of a trusted foreign callee are refused while the direct and parenthesised spellings stay clean
notes: specification/compatibility.mdx, 'Foreign Boundary': 'Trusted @throws {never} metadata opts out' of the checked panic case. That sentence is about the panic CHANNEL of a call. `SMITHERS1507` is a different obligation — a foreign call has to sit where lowering can preserve its evaluation order — and a marker that removes the panic case does not move the call to a safe position. So the answer here is not the panic rule at all, and that distinction is the case's content. WHY IT IS WORTH A CASE: the natural reading of 'trusted foreign calls are fine' is that a trusted callee is fine everywhere, and this program is where that reading is wrong. It also sits one token away from `selectors-over-local-and-trusted-values-stay-clean`, where a trusted foreign TAG selected by `??`, `||` and a conditional is CLEAN — the tag's operand is not in a call position the order rule governs — so the two cases together say the boundary is the call position and not the operator. That pair was measured, not assumed: an earlier draft of the negative case included `(double ?? localDouble)(2)` as a negative and both backends refused it, which is how this case came to exist. THE TWO CLEAN SPELLINGS ARE PART OF THE EXPECTATION even though they declare nothing: a `diagnostics` case is matched exactly, so a backend that refused `double(2)` or `(double)(3)` would add a diagnostic this expectation does not declare and the case would go red. They are the attribution control — without them the five refusals could be explained by `double` being foreign at all rather than by the selection. THE LOCAL ALTERNATE IS ON THE LEFT FOR `&&` AND THE COMMA and on the right for the rest, so a walk that reads only one operand is wrong on at least one row whichever side it reads. WHAT THIS CASE DELIBERATELY DOES NOT PIN: the message. `SMITHERS1507` carries one fixed remediation sentence, byte-identical on both backends, that names no part of this program. It also does not pin what happens when the callee is UNTRUSTED and selected — that draws this code and the panic-channel rules together, and pinning the combination here would make this file break for either cause. VERIFIED LOAD-BEARING, not assumed: mutating the declared column on line 18 — the `&&` row, whose trusted operand is on the RIGHT — from 43 to 42 (the column its `||` sibling reports) turns the case red on BOTH backends with the position diff printed, and the file was restored byte-identically (sha256 c63f347c7b573934ce6f1aec29cb2cb77c62c7e87b864a4927fa655940a13021 before and after, that digest being this file's content at the moment the mutation ran — the sentence recording it is appended afterwards, so the shipped file necessarily hashes differently).
